thread:
maria: Quick heads-up — nightly perf shows a host-side CPU spike around request parsing + a p99 bump on short-stream responses after yesterday's kernel-selector rollout. Seeing ~30% increase p99 for <=128-token streams.

kevin: Ugh, any flamegraphs or perf data?

maria: Putting the main traces here: https://perf.redwood/capture/9198765432 (private). Short summary: user-space parse/serialize time increased, and there's a tight cluster of small write syscalls from grpc that line up with the spikes.

maria: Top lines (sampling):
```
 22.1%  runtime  parse_request
 15.4%  grpc     grpc_writev
 10.2%  runtime  stream_chunker
  8.3%  kernel   futex_wait
  6.1%  runtime  kv_cache_miss_handler
```

diane: That kv_cache_miss_handler entry stands out — did the kernel selector change affect kv cache eviction patterns?

kevin: Possibly. The selector change pushed some models to a new tiled-kernel that has slightly different token-length prefetching. For short sequences it might be touching more memory paths. I can run an A/B and look at kvcache hit rates.

maria: kvcache hit-rate for these traces is ~92% normally, but for the regressed hosts we drop to ~78% during bursts. The timing shows miss+repopulate happens inline and stalls the parsing goroutine.

sam: Also noticed grpc small-write flood; the HTTP/2 framing + small application writes cause Nagle-ish behavior to hurt latency. We coalesced in a few places last quarter but the selector change touched the streaming hot path.

kevin: Can you paste the writev pattern?

maria: gist: `writev(3, [{...16B}, {...24B}, {...8B}], 3)` repeated w/ 4-7us gaps. Each call triggers grpc internals and syscall overhead.

kevin: Two cheap mitigations to test: 1) re-enable writev coalescing on the parse hotpath (we removed it in the refactor), 2) bump gRPC send buffer to encourage batching. Both are low-risk config/patches.

diane: For the kvcache, I suggest adding a tiny async repopulation: on miss, return partial and kick off a background fill so parse isn't blocked. We tried async-prefetch prototype before — helped p50/p95 but p99 was mixed.

maria: Agree on both. I ran a microbench: enabling writev coalesce locally reduced parse syscall time by ~40% and lowered p99 by ~12% on a tiny sample.

deploy-bot: Deployment 2026-03-21T02:13Z started for commit sha 7a1f9b2 (kernel-selector).

sam: If deploy coincides with the rollout, we should pin the selector until fixes land. Diane, can you open an issue and link the flamegraphs + the microbench snippets?

diane: On it. Created GH issue #4721: "host-parse + small-write p99 regression after kernel-selector rollout" with stack traces and initial findings. Assigned to kevin and sam.

kevin: I'll run the selector A/B and gather kvcache histograms (per-host) today. Also will PR the writev coalesce revert — small diff.

maria: I'll add a perf job that samples the host parse stacks at 10kHz for a short window during canary so we have better statistical power.

sam: I'll test the async kvcache prefill prototype against the canary. If we can't get p99 back within 24h we should rollback selector.

kevin: Quick note: kernel selector logs show a fallback path for models with seq_len<64 that hits a legacy codepath until the new microkernel warms up — that lines up with short streams being hit harder.

maria: Good catch. That explains both the extra memory touches and the write pattern changes (more small, immediate responses).

diane: Plan summary: 
- kevin: run A/B and PR writev coalesce revert (ETA 6h)
- sam: run async prefill experiment on canary (ETA 8h)
- maria: perf job + collect extended traces (ETA 3h)
- if no measurable p99 improvement within 24h -> rollback kernel-selector on canary hosts

kevin: ack, starting now.

maria: thanks. I'll post updates in this thread. :white_check_mark:
